newsitem.title: UK: UK insurers seen as easy Budget tax target.
newsitem.headline: UK insurers seen as easy Budget tax target.

text.p: UK insurers are an easy target for raising taxes in tomorrow's Budget, but believe insurance premium tax (IPT) should be left at four percent, industry sources said on Tuesday.

"We have made representations to the Chancellor (of the Exchequer) arguing against an increase as IPT impacts more heavily on lower earners," Malcolm Tarling, spokesman for the Association of British Insurers (ABI), told Reuters.

Industry sources said there have been no suggestions that IPT will be increased by Gordon Brown in his first Budget, but one company spokesman noted that the Chancellor is under pressure to raise tax by any means other than increasing income tax.
IPT was increased in April to 4.0 percent from 2.5 percent following an announcement in the last budget of the previous government.
A Reuters survey of Budget expectations showed that of 20 analysts polled, six expected a change in IPT and 14 saw no change.
IPT is levied on most non-life insurance policies, although a few, such as appliance guarantee policies, attract IPT at 17.5 percent.
Insurance analysts said that, in the long term, an increase to 17.5 percent is likely to bring Britain into line with some other European countries.
